title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
gist: A Stat analysis cited by Ars shows the MAHA PAC led by Tony Lyons raised only $3.2M (vs a touted $100M effort) and spent $10.5M in the midterm cycle, but under a tenth (~$1M) on independent expenditures for candidates, while spending heavily on steakhouses, a luxury DC club, allied media, security and its own nonprofit — undercutting claims MAHA's midterm wipeout was due to being outspent.

insights.claim: MAHA PAC raised just $3.2 million in the 2026 midterm cycle despite Tony Lyons announcing a $100 million fundraising effort, and spent over $10.5 million, more than $7 million from previously collected funds.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: MAHA's fundraising pull is far weaker than advertised, signaling limited political clout behind its health-policy agenda.
insights.locator: The findings are in stark contrast

insights.claim: Of MAHA PAC's $10.5 million midterm spending, only about $1 million went to independent expenditures on candidates, which OpenSecrets' Andrew Mayersohn calls unusual since major super PACs spend most on independent expenditures; over $700,000 of that targeted Sen. Bill Cassidy.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: The PAC functioned more as a patronage vehicle than an electoral force — discount MAHA electoral threats.
insights.quote: Major super PACs spend most of their money on independent expenditures.
insights.locator: Andrew Mayersohn, a committees researcher at OpenSecrets

insights.claim: MAHA PAC spent $49,900 backing Kevin Kiley in a race it called its most direct ideological confrontation, less than the $50,100 spent at Mastro's Steakhouse and under a third of $155,900 at Ned's Club; Kiley lost to pediatrician Richard Pan by double digits.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Electoral rejection of MAHA candidates suggests limited voter appetite for its anti-establishment health agenda.
insights.locator: In some cases, the scant political spending was dwarfed

insights.claim: MAHA PAC paid $500,000 to Phil McGraw's Merit Street Media, $275,000 to security firm Gavin de Becker & Associates (led by an ally of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.), tens of thousands to influencers and The MAHA Report writers, and over $3 million to its affiliated nonprofit MAHA Action.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Funds recycle within an allied media/influencer ecosystem; transparency questions could weaken RFK Jr.'s movement.
insights.locator: Outside of steaks and a private club
